title: p0-hostedapi-synthetic-load-staircase-investigation
content:
Summary:
On 2029-06-21 between ~03:12–03:48 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API streaming surface. Symptoms included elevated p50/p95/p99 latencies for streaming responses, a spike in 5xx errors on edge proxies (predominantly 502/504), and a rapid increase in KV cache eviction rates on a subset of host nodes. The issue coincided with an automated synthetic-load staircase test that ramped short-lived burst sessions (synthetic clients) across multiple regions to validate an autoscaler change.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: ~18% of streaming sessions in us-west-2 experienced either truncated streams or immediate 5xx replies for up to ~35 minutes. Non-streaming (batch generation) traffic mostly unaffected.
- Internal: Increased CPU on streaming acceptors, KV cache thrash leading to long tail latencies, edge proxy connection resets.
- Business: Temporary client retries and increased support tickets; no data loss.

Detection and Alerting:
- First alert: CTL streaming-p99-latency-us-west-2 breached threshold at 03:14 UTC (oncall page).
- Secondary: Edge 502-rate alarm triggered at 03:17 UTC.
- Observability: Spike in kv_cache_evictions/sec on nodes (dash: sres/kv-evict-overview).
- Pager: Oncall received P0 page at 03:18 UTC.

Timeline (condensed):
- 03:10 UTC: Synthetic staircase test job kicked off from infra-ci to validate autoscaler patch (note: job was supposed to target canary cluster only but had bad selector).
- 03:12 UTC: Short-lived synthetic streaming sessions begin across multiple clusters including production-serving pools.
- 03:14 UTC: First latency alert (stream p99).
- 03:17 UTC: Edge 502/504 alarm; oncall paged.
- 03:20 UTC: SREs rotate in and start triage (calls with infra-ci owner).
- 03:25 UTC: Observed KV cache eviction rate increase and cache miss amplification for streaming hot prefixes.
- 03:30 UTC: Mitigation 1: throttled synthetic-runner via CI abort; synthetic traffic reduced but backlog persisted due to eviction spiral.
- 03:36 UTC: Mitigation 2: Edge team applied temporary connection circuit-breaker to shed new streaming sessions to fallback tier.
- 03:48 UTC: Metrics returned toward baseline; edge 5xx reduced and streaming latencies stabilized.

Initial Hypotheses considered:
- Autoscaler misconfiguration caused hot shard thrash (later confirmed — job targeted prod pools accidentally).
- Model runtime bug provoking KV cache invalidation (ruled out after runtime team review).
- Edge proxy TLS handshake regressions (investigated; handshake rates nominal).

Root Cause (synthesis):
1) Human+CI selector bug: a synthetic-load staircase job (infra-ci) had an incorrect target selector that included production streaming pools rather than canary-only. The job exercised a high churn of short streaming sessions (connect/disconnect every ~8–14s).
2) Workload pattern mismatch: The bursty short-session pattern greatly increased KV cache churn (lots of prefix state and tiny per-session KV entries) causing eviction pressure. The serving runtime's eviction heuristics did not prioritize long-running customer sessions under this specific access pattern.
3) Cascading resource pressure: KV eviction amplified cache misses which led to more work per token; acceptor threads backed up, increasing streaming head latency and causing edge proxies to hit timeouts/circuit-break.

Why it became P0:
- The CI job targeted production by mistake and executed across regions simultaneously.
- Existing safeguards (rate-limits for CI jobs, canary-only selectors) were not applied due to a recent change in infra-ci templates.
- The runtime's eviction policy lacked a simple long-session priority knob and the autoscaler reacted in a way that briefly reduced headroom.

Immediate Mitigations applied during incident:
- Abort synthetic job in CI (03:30 UTC) — primary mitigation.
- Edge circuit-breaker to send new streaming requests to fallback tier (03:36 UTC) to reduce admission pressure.
- Temporarily increased KV cache high-water mark on impacted pools (03:38 UTC) to avoid additional evictions while stability recovered. Note: this change is coarse and reverted after recovery for safety.

Recovery and Verification:
- After abort + edge fallback, p99 streaming latencies trended down over 12 minutes; 5xx rates normalized by 03:48 UTC.
- Verified no model degradation using smoke prompts; customer-facing traffic sampled for correctness.

Post-incident Analysis / Diffs from normal ops:
- The eviction amplification is the key fragility: small, repeated connections with small working sets caused disproportionate eviction churn.
- Autoscaler and CI safety checks were both necessary — failing one allowed the cascade.

Immediate action items (owner -> owner, rough ETA):
- infra-ci: add and enforce canary-only label in staircase test templates; add preflight selector validation (owner: Priya Singh, ETA: 2029-07-02).
- CI ops: add an explicit rate-limit and cross-check gate for any job that can target 'prod' pools (owner: Marcus O'Neill, ETA: 2029-07-05).
- Runtime: add short-term guard in eviction logic to prefer session-age over absolute access recency when evicting small entries (owner: Lina Martinez, ETA: prototype 2029-07-08).
- Edge: formalize streaming fallback policy and automate toggles (owner: Ethan Park, ETA: 2029-07-01).
- SRE: Add alerting for synthetic-job-originated traffic (detect CI user-agent patterns) and auto-suppress if a known test is running (owner: Avery Chen, ETA: 2029-07-03).

Runbook Draft (playbook for future similar incidents):
1) Identification:
   - Check synthetic job dashboard (infra-ci) for live runs. Query: label:staircase OR job:synthetic-staircase active > 0
   - Open sres/hostedapi/streaming dashboard; check p95/p99, kv_cache_evictions/sec, acceptor_queue_depth.
2) Immediate containment:
   - If CI synthetic job present -> abort job (CI console) and confirm job stopped.
   - If edge 5xx > threshold -> toggle streaming fallback (edge-cfg toggle streaming.fallback=true) to shed new sessions.
   - Increase KV cache high-water mark on impacted pool via k8s/serving-config override (note: apply briefly).
3) Stabilization:
   - Monitor kv_cache_evictions/sec and acceptor depth; wait for two stabilization windows (5 minute sliding windows) before reverting coarse cache override.
   - Gradually re-enable traffic; watch p99.
4) Root cause collection:
   - Collect runtime logs for acceptor threads (last 1 hour), KV eviction traces, CI job run log, and edge proxy logs. Attach to JIRA ticket.

Runbook - quick commands (internal):
- Abort CI job: infra-ci cancel-job --id <job-id>
- Toggle edge fallback: edge-admin set-config streaming.fallback=true --zone <zone>
- Increase kv cache HW mark: kubectl -n serving patch configmap serving-runtime --patch '{"data":{"kv_cache_hw":"0.85"}}'

Monitoring / Alert changes proposed:
- New synthetic-origin alert: detect sudden uptick in requests with user_agent:infra-ci-staircase and page SRE oncall if > X rps for 2m.
- KV eviction ratio alert: tie eviction/sec to session_count; fire if eviction/session > 0.02 for 3m.
- Edge 5xx correlation: graph edge-502-rate vs kv_cache_evictions with a runbook link in alert payload.

Longer-term engineering changes suggested:
- Runtime: smarter eviction policy (session-age bias + minimum residency for streaming-session keys). Full implementation + tests (owner: Lina Martinez, ETA: 2029-08-15).
- CI infra: introduce declarative job scopes; disallow selectors without explicit scope field=canary|prod and require manual approval for any job that targets prod (owner: Priya Singh, ETA: 2029-07-22).
- Simulator: Expand chaos-sim tests to include synthetic staircase pattern in staging to exercise eviction heuristics before merging autoscaler changes. (owner: SRE-runbooks team, ETA: 2029-07-30).
- Observability: add a dimension to streaming telemetry to mark synthetic vs real sessions so we can silence noisy tests from customer-impacting alerts.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Were there any other CI jobs with similar bad selectors in the last 90 days? (action: infra-ci audit)
- How do long-running customer sessions behave under the new proposed eviction heuristic? Need perf matrix and regression tests.
- Can we automate graceful backpressure from runtime to edge when KV eviction crosses threshold?

Postmortem status: Draft. Next steps: circulate to runtime, infra-ci, and edge teams for technical review and cost/rollback tolerances. Target final postmortem + follow-ups board by 2029-07-10.

Notes to self / oncall perspective:
- Keep a small checklist in the oncall binder: abort-ci-job -> edge-fallback -> increase-kv-hwm -> monitor. That sequence cut the incident from 45 -> 18 minutes in practice.
- For future P0 drills, simulate short-lived streaming bursts (8–20s session pattern) not just steady-state high QPS.

Attachments / references (internal):
- infra-ci run log snapshot: /mnt/artifacts/infra-ci/2029-06-21/staircase-run-3492.log
- Grafana dashboard links: sres/hostedapi/streaming (panel ids included in ticket JIRA-INC-3982)
- Runtime PR that touched eviction heuristics last month: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pulls/4103

Reviewed: Priya, Marcus, Lina, Ethan (pending)
